subject: Critical Success Markers & A/B Acceptance Suite for Pilot Wrap (MAP)
messages:
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@neurolytix.ai>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: lauren.price@neurolytix.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot MAP — high level success asks

Aisha,

Thanks for the demo today — the team liked the latency profile and the private deployment option. Before we commit to an internal pilot, leadership asked for a concise list of measurable success markers and what you would run as acceptance tests. Specifically they want:

- Primary success metric (production analogue)
- Exit gates (what causes a fail/stop)
- A/B acceptance test plan and sample test cases
- Timeline to close if gates are met

Can you sketch this out so we can build our internal sign‑off? We can loop in our infra lead if you want to align on KV cache and prefix caching assumptions.

—Daniel
Director of Product, Neurolytix

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@neurolytix.ai>
Cc: lauren.price@neurolytix.ai, ben_carter@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP — high level success asks

Daniel — thanks for the quick note. Attached is a draft MAP spreadsheet (MAP-Neurolytix-v1.xlsx) and a short eval-test-cases.pdf that maps each acceptance test to a production signal. High level summary below; full details in the attachment.

SUMMARY (short):
- Primary success metric: mean latency P90 < 220ms for 1k concurrent users with 4k token median prompt under a dedicated capacity profile.
- Quality guardrail: semantic correctness >= 92% on curated prompt set (annotated pass/fail).
- Cost guardrail: token cost delta vs baseline model <= +18% (we model throughput savings separately).
- Exit gates: sustained P90 > 400ms for 30m OR semantic correctness < 85% on >3 sequential audit prompts OR inability to scale to the agreed concurrency within 2 provision windows.
- A/B acceptance suite: 1200 prompts split across 3 buckets (accuracy, hallucination-resilience, safety). Run A = your current inference stack, B = Redwood dedicated run with prefix caching/quantization profile Q2.
- Timeline: 3-week evaluation window, decision at EOW (week 3) with optional 1-week remediation run if borderline. Close to MSA if gates pass and DocuSign signed.

Next steps: Ben — can you drop the proposed runbook and sample workload configuration? Tessa — I'll draft the mutual action plan milestones and DocuSign milestone language. Daniel — can you confirm the target concurrency number (we used 1k as placeholder) and whether your infra team needs a run-through on KV assumptions?

Regards,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: MAP-Neurolytix-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 110KB); eval-test-cases.pdf (doc, 56KB)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com, daniel.cho@neurolytix.ai
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, lauren.price@neurolytix.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Sep 2025 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP — high level success asks

Quick technical runbook (summary):

- Config: dedicated pool, 4x A100 equivalent, model variant redwood-open-7b-q4 (quantized profile Q2).
- Batching: continuous batching target = 32ms window / max batch 256 tokens.
- KV cache: prefix caching enabled for repetitive prompts; warm-start phase of 2 hours recommended to populate user-level prefixes.
- Monitoring signals to collect: per‑request latency, token count, cache hit ratio, model confidence score, error rate (4xx/5xx), and top-5 token divergence vs baseline.
- A/B runner: we'll run the A/B harness on a mirrored dataset; B will be instrumented with tracing to link tokens to latency and cost.

Failures to watch for (exit triggers):
- Cache miss ratio > 90% on warm-start profiles after 2 hours
- Error rate spike > 1% sustained for 10 minutes
- Token divergence causing semantic drop (see eval doc)

I attached a lightweight CSV with the suggested A/B prompt mix and scripts to run the harness (A-B-run-results.csv will collect run outputs). Happy to do a 30m call with Neurolytix infra next week to align.

—Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: A-B-run-results.csv (template)

From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@neurolytix.ai>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: lauren.price@neurolytix.ai, ben_carter@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP — high level success asks

Aisha / Ben — this looks good and concrete, thanks. Confirming: target concurrency should be 800 sustained users (peaks to 1k). Our infra lead prefers the warm-start window to be 3 hours; they can join the alignment call.

Two quick asks from our side before we lock the MAP:
1) Can you add a lightweight regression check that flags hallucination rate by entity type (PHI / device ids)? We need to track safety regressions separately.
2) On remediation cadence, can we bake in a canary rollback step (automated fallback to the baseline model) if semantic correctness drops >5% during rollout?

If you can update the MAP sheet with those items and confirm a 3-week window vs the 2-week we discussed, we can move to internal procurement review.

—Daniel

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@neurolytix.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com, lauren.price@neurolytix.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 17:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP — high level success asks

Thanks — updated the MAP spreadsheet to reflect your asks and bumped warm-start to 3 hours and window to 3 weeks. Key updates (changes shown inline in the sheet):

- Hallucination/PHI check: added a breakdown in eval-test-cases.pdf and a daily regression script that samples 200 responses and flags entity‑level hallucination rate. Threshold: PHI hallucination < 0.5% and device-id hallucination < 1%.
- Canary rollback: added automated fallback policy in the runbook: if semantic correctness drops >5% or P90 > 350ms for 10m, system falls back to baseline model for affected route while engineers triage.
- Final decision checkpoint: EOD Friday of week 3 — if all gates pass we move to draft MSA and procurement; otherwise we run a 1-week remediation window (instrumentation + tuning).

Next steps: Daniel — I'll request a short procurement checklist from finance and start the DocuSign template. Ben / Tessa — please review the updated acceptance tests and confirm the A/B harness schedule; propose two 2-hour windows next week for the actual run.

Regards,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | https://redwood.inference
Attachments: MAP-Neurolytix-v1.xlsx (updated), eval-test-cases.pdf (updated)
